access: Author/coordinator only; withhold from grammar agent and independent solver until their solutions are frozen.
origin: new_teaching_material; translation models of all exact source prompts

items.prompt_original: Gold is more precious (64) than silver.
items.model: Gold is dēorwierðre ðonne seolfor.
audit_notes: Comparative predicate is weak neuter singular; no superlative is substituted.

items.prompt_original: Righteousness is more precious than gold.
items.model: Rihtwīsnes is dēorwierðre ðonne gold.
audit_notes: Comparative predicate is weak feminine singular with rihtwīsnes.

items.prompt_original: The bath is hot.
items.model: Ðæt bæð is hāt.

items.prompt_original: The baths are hot.
items.model: Ðā baðu sindon hāt.
audit_notes: Long hāt has endingless strong neuter plural; baðu is neuter plural.

items.prompt_original: The animals are living.
items.model: Ðā dēor sindon cwicu.

items.prompt_original: Some pearls are black.
items.model: Suma męregrēotan sindon blaca.

items.prompt_original: The island is beautiful.
items.model: Ðæt īgland is fæger.

items.prompt_original: Dolphins swim through the water.
items.model: Męreswīn swimmað þurh ðæt wæter.
audit_notes: Original indefinite dolphins has no required article; ðurh governs accusative.

items.prompt_original: Here are fishes often caught.
items.model: Hēr sindon fiscas oft fangen.
audit_notes: Selected fōn catch takes the ordinary patient in active and passive; bare past participle permitted by prior predicate-participle variation and newly supplied lexical pair.

items.prompt_original: The night is more beautiful than the day.
items.model: Sēo niht is fægerre ðonne se dæg.

items.prompt_original: The city was distinguished with walls and gates.
items.model: Sēo ceaster wæs geweorðod mid weallum and gatum.
audit_notes: Original says was, not is. Walls and gates are dative after instrumental mid.

items.prompt_original: Summer comes, and then winter.
items.model: Sumer cymð, and ðonne cymð winter.
audit_notes: Repeating cymð makes the original elliptical second predicate explicit without changing its meaning.

items.prompt_original: The sun shines over all.
items.model: Sēo sunne scīnð ofer eall.
audit_notes: Eall is substantival neuter accusative singular everything, not an unmarked invented singular noun.

items.prompt_original: The old man came to the house.
items.model: Se ealda mann cōm tō ðǣm hūse.

items.prompt_original: Here are also found lead and iron.
items.model: Hēr sindon ēac lēad and īsern funden.

items.prompt_original: Put not your hand into the fire.
items.model: Ne dō ðīne hand on ðæt fȳr.
audit_notes: Singular addressee chosen; on plus accusative gives the goal of placing. Full hand paradigm already supplies endingless accusative.

items.prompt_original: The soldier takes the gem.
items.model: Se cęmpa nimð ðone gimm.

items.prompt_original: The rain injures the tower.
items.model: Se regn scęðeð ðǣm torre.
audit_notes: Tower is dative with scęððan; final selected third singular spelling must match grammar audit.

items.prompt_original: The whale swims.
items.model: Se hwæl swimð.

items.prompt_original: Fishermen caught seals.
items.model: Fisceras fēngon sēolas.

items.prompt_original: The hungry sheep are not fed.
items.model: Ðā hungrigan scēap ne sindon fēded.
audit_notes: Weak hungrigan agrees with plural neuter scēap; this is a passive statement, not a negative command.

items.prompt_original: The man’s wife is beautiful.
items.model: Ðæs mannes wīf is fæger.

items.prompt_original: Some men are black.
items.model: Sume męnn sindon blace.

items.prompt_original: The carpenter will clothe his son.
items.model: Se trēowwyrhta scrȳt his sunu.
audit_notes: Present scrȳt has future reference licensed by the English task; no untaught infinitive of scrȳdan is silently promoted.

items.prompt_original: Depart from me, for I am (om. a) sinful man, (om. O) Lord.
items.model: Gewīt fram mē, for-ðon-ðe ic eom synfull mann, Dryhten.
audit_notes: Singular command route; original omission controls do not remove ordinary bare predicate mann. Dryhten is direct address.

items.prompt_original: They shall drink, but ye shall be thirsty.
items.model: Hīe drincað, ac gē bēoð ðurstige.
audit_notes: Simple presents can bear the indicated future reference; adjective ðurstige agrees with the addressed plural, with ordinary copula.

items.prompt_original: He said to her, Give me, I beseech thee, water to drink; for I am thirsty.
items.model: Hē sægde hiere: Sęle mē, ic bidde ðē, wæter drincan; for-ðon-ðe ic eom ðurstig.
audit_notes: Give-to-drink remains the explicitly supplied whole construction from Unit10, with plain drincan and no tō. Biddan selects accusative person ðē; parenthetic clause retained.

items.prompt_original: He is not (om. a) God of (om. the) dead, but of (om. the) living.
items.model: Hē nis God dēadra, ac cwicra.
audit_notes: Bare strong generic genitive plurals dēadra/cwicra; no unintroduced libbende system.

items.prompt_original: The sun shines on (ofer) the righteous and the unrighteous.
items.model: Sēo sunne scīnð ofer ðā rihtwīsan and ðā unrihtwīsan.

items.prompt_original: Ye are (om. the) light of the world.
items.model: Gē sindon ðǣre worulde lēoht.
audit_notes: Ðǣre worulde is the ordinary genitive the world; bare lēoht is the predicate.

items.prompt_original: The twelve gates were twelve pearls.
items.model: Ðā twęlf gatu wǣron twęlf męregrēotan.

items.prompt_original: The street of the city was gold.
items.model: Ðǣre ceastre strǣt wæs gold.

items.prompt_original: Those that ate were four thousand men (154. c), besides women and children.
items.model: Ðā ðe ǣton wǣron fēower ðūsend manna, būtan wīfum and bearnum.
audit_notes: The full fēower ðūsend manna phrase is supplied, with explicit higher-numeral government; būtan governs the following datives.

items.prompt_original: Blessed (p.p.) be God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort.
items.model: Geblētsod sīe God, ūres Dryhtnes Hǣlendes Crīstes Fæder, mildheortnessa Fæder and ealre frōfre God.
audit_notes: Independent blessing: sīe is optative present subjunctive. Proper title Hǣlendes and Crīstes stand in apposition to Dryhtnes. Ealre agrees with genitive feminine frōfre.

items.prompt_original: The winds were favorable.
items.model: Ðā windas wǣron gesyndige.

items.prompt_original: He wishes to watch their journey.
items.model: Hē wille hiera sīðfæt scēawian.
audit_notes: The subject is he and the possessor their; wishes is volitional willan with plain infinitive scēawian.

items.prompt_original: The wind and the sea obey him.
items.model: Se wind and se sǣ hīerað him.
audit_notes: Sea uses the actual prior masculine paradigm; the coordinated subject takes plural hīerað and obey governs dative him.

items.prompt_original: Not at all in vain fought I with death, as he fought with beasts.
items.model: Nālæs hōlunga feaht ic wið dēað, swā hē feaht wið dēor.
audit_notes: Bounded nālæs hōlunga phrase conveys not at all in vain; selected wið+accusative opponents. Swā-swā is the assigned as comparison, not inasmuch as.

items.prompt_original: The time draws near [approaches, 164] (om. the) birth of Christ.
items.model: Sēo tīd genēalǣcð Crīstes gebyrde.
audit_notes: The time is nominative subject; gebyrde is dative complement of approach, and Crīstes is genitive dependent on birth.

items.prompt_original: It is the day when (ðe) he was born (ācenned).
items.model: Hit is se dæg ðe hē wæs ācenned.
audit_notes: Exact source hint ācenned has plain e; supplied passive participle, without a full new ācennan system.

items.prompt_original: O, wast thou with me, dearest, then, while I rose up against my doom (dōm)?
items.model: Ēalā, wǣre ðū mid mē, lēofosta, ðā, ðā-hwīle-ðe ic rās ūp ongēan mīnne dōm?
audit_notes: Then, while, up and against are all retained. Wǣre is second singular preterite indicative in the direct past question, not automatically subjunctive. Weak personal direct address lēofosta needs its bounded address frame.

items.prompt_original: The moon is hid (hȳdan, 113), the night is still.
items.model: Se mōna is hȳded, sēo niht is stillu.
audit_notes: Positive stillu is strong feminine nominative singular; e-class dictionary final e does not eliminate the -u ending.

items.prompt_original: Thou bringst the fisher to his wife.
items.model: Ðū bringst ðone fiscere tō his wīfe.
audit_notes: Bringan takes accusative traveller and tō+dative destination/person.

items.prompt_original: Calm is the morn(ing).
items.model: Smylte is se morgen.

items.prompt_original: I know that this was life.
items.model: Ic wāt ðæt ðis wæs līf.
audit_notes: Life is līf; original does not say wife or wile.

items.prompt_original: What do ye more than they?
items.model: Hwæt dōð gē mā ðonne hīe?
audit_notes: Mā is amount adverb; comparative standard hīe is nominative with do understood. Hwæt is object of dōð.
